title: SLO-driven dependency facade: optimistic hedged reads, soft-circuit state, and tenant-aware shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Intermittent downstream degradation (Redis/TLS proxies, Kafka brokers, and Postgres read-replicas) has caused tail-latency spikes and cross-tenant availability regressions. Existing approaches (hard circuit breakers or blunt global shedding) are either too aggressive or too slow to react, resulting in SLA misses for critical customers and noisy escalations.

Goal: Implement a dependency facade that sits between the request admission layer and downstream clients. The facade implements SLO-driven behavior: optimistic hedged reads, soft-state circuit breakers that decay gradually, tenant-aware load-shedding priorities, and per-region fast-fail policies for multi-region failover. The facade should reduce P99 latency during partial outages and keep critical traffic flowing while isolating noisy tenants.

Scope: Server-side proxy logic in the request path for text-gen and embed routes (hosted + dedicated). Work includes runtime changes to the gateway, connection pool adjustments, per-tenant scoring/priority, feature flags, observability (SLO-aligned metrics and traces), automated experiments, and runbook/playbook updates. Does NOT include persistent-store schema changes or customer-facing API changes.
acceptance_criteria: H1: 30% reduction in P99 tail latency during simulated downstream slowdowns for critical routes (text-generation) in staging compared to baseline
H2: Tenant QPS prioritization prevents customer-tier P99 SLOs from regressing while low-priority tenants are degraded under overload
H3: Circuit soft-state transitions (healthy -> degraded -> recovery) are visible in dashboards and match thresholds defined in the design doc
H4: Automated chaos tests (Redis/Kafka/DB latency injection) run in CI and validate hedged-read fallbacks and region failover behavior
updates: 2026-02-25 - Aisha Patel: Ticket created after post-incident retrofit workshop (incident 2026-02-20). Initial design sketch completed; recommended hedged-read + soft-circuit hybrid. Assigned to Marco.

2026-03-02 - Marco Ruiz: Prototype runtime changes landed in feature branch: optimistic hedges for KV GET path, soft-circuit state machine with backoff windows. Unit tests + bench harness added. Observability hooks instrumented for circuit state and hedged latency histograms.
2026-03-05 - Sophie Chen (SRE): Load test in staging (partial Redis node slowdown) shows 18% P99 improvement; noted CPU increase on gateway under hedging—added follow-up to tune thread pools.
2026-03-07 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented tenant-priority scoreboard and per-tenant admission buckets. Added metric 'dep_facade.admit_skipped_by_tenant' and 'dep_facade.priority_drop_count'.

2026-03-09 - Design review with PM and SRE: agreed thresholds for 'soft-degrade' (start shedding at 85% of SLO burn rate) and recovery decay window (exponential decay with 10m half-life). Linked design doc for sign-off.

2026-03-12 - Marco Ruiz: Canary rollout to 10% traffic in us-east-1 (non-critical customers). Early telemetry: P99 down 27% for canary users during injected 200ms datastore latency; non-canary unaffected. Preparing broader canary and failover drills week of 2026-03-16.
comments: SRE Lead (Sophie Chen): Please ensure the runbook includes exact rollback criteria. If P95 or P99 for high-tier customers degrades by >5% during rollout, rollback immediately.
PM (Liam O'Connor): Prioritize ensuring critical customers are in the high-tier list before canary expands. Work with account managers to confirm list.
Infra (Devon Park): Noted additional memory use in gateway with hedging buffers; recommended a cap and LRU eviction to avoid OOMs under pathological workloads.
QA (Nina Alvarez): Added tests to the chaos suite to simulate regional blackout and verify that hedged-reads don't amplify cross-region traffic unexpectedly.
